Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's reply. The two umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley will open the innings for England. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Off we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

Right then, this game is nicely poised with four sessions remaining in the Test. With Nathan Lyon unlikely to bowl, the Aussie pace attack will be expected to fill that void. On the other hand, England have the resources to get over the line here and bring the series back on level terms. Can the English batters rise to the challenge? We shall find out as the players return for the final session of Day 4 in a bit.

With a lead of 221 runs, Cameron Green and Alex Carey started the second session steadily for Australia. However, they lost both set batters in quick succession which put the visitors in a spot of bother. They seemed to have no answer to England's short-ball approach and found it very hard to stay at the crease. That said, Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins stuck at it and provided their side with valuable runs. Moreover, Nathan Lyon was in a lot of pain but braved his calf injury to provide able support to Mitchell Starc. At the start of Day 4, Australia would have fancied themselves a lead in excess of 400 but 370 is still a daunting total.

Australia have been bowled out for 279 in their second innings! Ben Stokes will be pleased with the fight shown by his bowlers and England now need 371 runs to win and draw level in the series! Having been at the receiving end in the first innings, England kept directing short-pitched stuff in the two sessions of Day 4 and certainly gave Australia a taste of their own medicine. Every English pacer ran in and peppered the visitors with short balls and never allowed any of the opposition batters to settle in. Stuart Broad was the pick of the bowlers with four wickets while Josh Tongue and Ollie Robinson accounted for two wickets each.

OUT! TAKEN! Stuart Broad gets his fourth and that will be the end of Australia! Nathan Lyon's brave effort comes to an end now. Stuart Broad bangs in a sharp bouncer, on middle, Nathan Lyon backs away and tries to pull but gets a top edge as the ball goes in the air, Ben Stokes at short mid-wicket settles under it and pouches it safely. So, the target for England will be 371 runs!

SHORT, SHORT, and SHORT! This was the plan employed by the English pacers and it worked for them quite well but they had to be patient and credit goes to them for sticking with their plan. Day 4 started with Usman Khawaja and Steven Smith looking solid as ever with conditions also good for batting. After a few overs, the hosts decided to go with the short-ball plan which was the downfall for them in their first innings. However, before drinks, both the batters managed to avoid any sort of trouble, but soon after the break Khawaja finally succumbed to the short ball and Smith followed him in the next over as well. Travis Head was also dismissed with a splendid catch from Root at short leg which also made him the highest catch-taker on the field for England in Tests. It was Stuart Broad again with two crucial wickets while Josh Tongue got one. Cameron Green and Alex Carey saw out the rest of the session and will look to build on that while the hosts will hope to take the three wickets quickly in the post-Lunch session as it does not likely that Nathan Lyon will come out to bat. Join us for the second session at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 92 runs and 3 wickets in 28.2 overs. A bit of a shared session but overall the Aussies are much ahead in the game. England managed to get the breakthroughs but the runs also kept flowing and the visitors lead by 313 runs now.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries to end the session! Shortens his length and bowls it just outside off, Cameron Green rises and punches it through covers. Gets enough bat on it and the ball trickles to the fence for four more runs. That will be Lunch on Day 4!

On the flip side, Australia were off to the best possible start on Day 3 as Mitchell Starc struck in his very first over. The Aussie pace attack went all out with the short ball barrage and dismantled the English batting unit. Having come out to bat in testing conditions, the visitors were successful in keeping the English bowlers at bay and stretched their lead to 221 runs before rain brought an abrupt end to the day. With plenty of batting still to come, Australia will look to step on the gas and then take a call on a declaration late in the day. Will Australia continue to pile more misery on England? We shall find out soon, as the first ball on Day 4 is not far away.

Having started Day 3, trailing by 138 runs, England lost Ben Stokes on the second ball of the day which put them in early trouble. The hosts surrendered themselves to the short ball ploy by the Aussie pacers, losing the last six wickets for 47 runs. In the second essay, English bowlers began well and kept testing the two Aussie openers by bowling in the right channels. That said, they could only succeed in picking a couple of wickets and will have their work cut out on Day 4.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 4 of the second Test between England and Australia at the Lord's in London. We have had three days of entertaining action with the game ebbing and flowing, and it is Australia who find themselves in a strong position to call the shots.

Right then, that is all the action from Day 3 where Australia dominated proceedings and also have a healthy lead. It will be interesting to see how both teams execute their plans on Day 4 which will start on July 1, Saturday at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build up. Cheers!

England, on the other hand would want to forget their batting performance in the first session as they lost six wickets for just 47 runs and surrendered a 91-lead to the visitors. However, they showed grit and determination with their bowling with not much to show. Stuart Broad looked the most dangerous and troubled Marnus Labuschagne throughout his innings but he didn't get any wickets. James Anderson got rid of Marnus while it was a peach from Josh Tongue to dismiss David Warner again in this Test. They could have got Marnus out earlier but Ben Stokes did not review a LBW shout which Ball Tracking later showed three reds. All of their bowlers bowled well but the luck was just not on their side and they will look to make amends at the start of Day 4.

Australia well and truly dominated the 'Moving Day' right from the start and this Test has tilted in their favour massively now. They got off to a dream start as Mitchell Starc removed the opposition skipper on the second ball of the Day which set the tone for them. Pat Cummins, Travis Head and Josh Hazlewood all contributed with the wickets as they bowled out the hosts in the first session itself. Their openers then saw out the rest of the session without any trouble. However, they lost David Warner early in the second session but Usman Khawaja continued his fine form and notched up another fifty while Marnus Labuschagne supported him well despite surviving a few scares but ultimately got out to a poor shot. After that, Steven Smith walked in to join Khawaja and both of them kept the English bowlers at bay, but just an hour or so into the third session the rain came in and the umpires decided to stop the game.

Bad news folks! We will have no further play on Day 3 as rain played spoilsport. It is Stumps on Day 3. Session Summary - 49 runs and 1 wicket in 13.4 overs. Australia lead by 221 runs and are in a very good position.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 3. The English players make their way out to the middle followed by the two Aussie batters. Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne will resume the innings for Australia. It will be James Anderson to start the proceedings with the ball for England. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

After a mediocre first session on Day 3, English bowlers started well with the ball in the second session. Stuart Broad and James Anderson used the conditions to their advantage and kept hitting probing lines and lengths consistently. They did concede an odd boundary here and there but were clinical overall. Coming off an impressive showing in the first innings, Josh Tongue accounted for David Warner in the second innings as well and gave his side a much-needed breakthrough. He and Ollie Robinson stuck at it and did not allow the Aussie batters to release the pressure. With conditions expected to remain gloomy at Lord's, England will be hoping for some early inroads in the third session. Do join us back at 8.30 pm IST (3.00 pm GMT) for another riveting session of Test cricket.

SESSION SUMMARY: 69 runs, 26 overs and one wicket. An eventful end to the session, one that has belonged to Australia! Having done well to negotiate the tricky phase before Lunch, David Warner and Usman Khawaja picked up where they left off in the first session. Both batters applied themselves well under testing conditions and gave a good account of themselves. They were quick to pounce on loose deliveries and by doing so, did not let themselves get bogged down. Despite losing Warner, Khawaja stood firm at one end and is now five runs short of yet another fifty. Marnus Labuschange has had a couple of nervous moments ever since his arrival and he will look to start afresh with Usman Khawaja in the final session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 59 runs and 6 wickets in 21.2 overs. Australia have dominated this session and stamped their authority in this Test as they are much ahead at the moment.
